title: SDK call circuitry and schema safeguard helpers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: SDK users across Python/TypeScript/Go need robust, consistent helpers for invoking model-invoked functions/tools. Current SDKs have duplicated patterns across languages: naive schema validation that hard-fails on small mismatches, inconsistent retry semantics for function calls vs plain generation, poor streaming ergonomics when function outputs are emitted incrementally, and few helpers for idempotency or partial replays. This ticket delivers a cross-SDK "call circuitry" layer: a small, opinionated set of helpers that validate/coerce function payloads, apply safe retry / circuit-breaking behavior, assemble streaming chunks into typed results, and emit diagnostics that tie back to Console telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Publish language-native helpers in Python, TypeScript, and Go that expose a small, consistent surface: validate_call_schema(), invoke_with_safety(), stream_to_struct(), and idempotent_call_token()
Helpers perform non-destructive coercion where safe (e.g., numeric strings -> numbers) and return a structured ValidationReport when coercion or warnings occur rather than throwing by default
invoke_with_safety() implements configurable retry/backoff policies that are aware of function-calling semantics (no retry for non-idempotent side-effect flags unless idempotency token provided)
stream_to_struct() can rehydrate chunked function responses into final typed objects and provides a streaming iterator API in each language
Telemetry hooks are added so Console can display per-call validation warnings and retry counts (events emitted via existing SDK diagnostics channel)
Comprehensive unit + integration tests covering schema edge cases, streaming interruptions, and retry behavior in SDK CI
implementation_notes: Design: keep core semantics language-agnostic and implement a thin adapter per SDK. Core rules: 1) Validation layers emit a ValidationReport with fields (valid:bool, errors:[], warnings:[], coerced_payload:str) rather than throwing by default. 2) invoke_with_safety() accepts: payload, schema, idempotency_token (optional), retry_policy (enum: default/strict/none), side_effects (enum: none/possible/guaranteed). 3) Default policy: allow standard network/timeouts retries for transient network errors, but suppress retries for guaranteed side_effects unless idempotency_token is present. 4) Streaming: stream_to_struct() must support incremental JSON/Text reassembly and a tolerant parser that copes with partial JSON tokens and recovers on reconnect. 5) Add an opt-in strict_mode that raises on first validation error for customers who prefer fail-fast. Implementation steps: - build shared design doc and test vectors (json schemas + example outputs) - implement core semantics in TypeScript package (reference impl) - port to Python and Go with ergonomic surfaces - wire telemetry events to diagnostics channel - update SDK docs and examples
testing_steps: Unit tests: validation coercion table (numeric strings, nullables, enum case-insensitive)
Integration test: simulated streaming function that emits JSON in 3 partial chunks; ensure stream_to_struct() yields final typed object and that intermediate states are available via iterator
Retry tests: simulated transient failures that succeed after 1 retry; assert retry count is emitted in telemetry and final result returned
Non-idempotent test: function flagged as guaranteed side_effects; call without idempotency token should not retry on server-side 500 and should surface proper error
Cross-language parity checks: run the same test vectors against Python, TypeScript, and Go helpers and confirm ValidationReport shape and behavior match
rollout_plan: Phase 1: land TypeScript reference implementation behind experimental flag + docs snippets (2 weeks). Phase 2: port to Python and Go and add cross-SDK conformance tests (3 weeks). Phase 3: flip default for new SDKs to opt-out strict_mode and announce in release notes; provide migration guide for customers relying on fail-fast behavior. Monitor Console telemetry for validation_warning spikes after rollout and pre-announce to customers using Private/Dedicated with high volume.
notes: Spike found that some model tool outputs include trailing commas and single quotes; tolerant parser will normalize before schema validation.
Telemetry event names: sdk.invoke.validation_warning, sdk.invoke.retry, sdk.invoke.idempotency_used
Consider adding circuit-breaker metrics to Console per-customer request rate if retry storms occur
comments: 2025-02-18 - Liam Chen: Started TS reference implementation. Key open question: should ValidationReport be a separate API object or returned as metadata on response? Leaning toward metadata to keep callsite plumbing small.
2025-02-21 - Marco Rivera (PM): For Dedicated customers we should add a toggle to force strict_mode at org level—helps enterprises that require deterministic rejections.
2025-02-25 - Priya Nair (SRE): In canary we saw 0.3% more validation_warnings leading to a small spike in error logs; recommend sampling warnings at 10% in initial rollout.
2025-02-28 - Design review (Aisha): Added streaming UX notes — expose partial object preview in SDK iterators so apps can show progressive UI while final validation happens.
